caption: Causal Link
description: A binding from this event to the operation that caused it. Written by the system that recorded this event, which generally did not observe the causing operation and knows only the identifier it was given and the way that identifier reached it. The binding is an unverified assertion by the causing party, faithfully persisted: attribution_method_id records how the recording system learned the identifier, not that the claim behind it is true. The identifier is resolved within the namespace of the system that issued it, named by issuer_uid; an identifier that is not globally unique cannot be resolved without it. Where an operation is retried, uid names the call whose request the system acted on, so a retried operation resolves to a single record rather than one per attempt.
name: causal_link

issuer_uid.caption: Issuing System ID
issuer_uid.description: The unique identifier of the system that issued uid, naming the namespace the identifier is resolvable within. Required in practice whenever uid is not globally unique on its own: a distributed tracing span identifier, for example, is unique within its trace rather than universally, so a consumer given the value alone cannot resolve it to one operation. Omitting it asserts that uid is self-describing and globally resolvable.

uid.caption: Causing Operation ID
uid.description: The unique identifier of the operation this event is attributed to, as recorded by the system that performed it. The value crosses a trust boundary rather than being generated here; the recording system persists what it was given, without having observed the operation the identifier names.
